title: dynamic-batching: sequence-length bucketing + padding-minimization heuristics (v5)
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: persistent padding in continuous-batching paths increases GPU work and unit cost for real-world request distributions with long tail sequence lengths. This PR extends our previous bucketing efforts with a histogram-driven bucketing strategy, an adaptive padding threshold, and scheduler hooks to prefer low-padding batches while preserving latency SLOs.

What this changes: one continuous JSON string describing the change set, design and results. Design summary: 1) Collect online per-worker sequence-length histograms (exponentially decayed) to capture current request mix. 2) Compute bucketing boundaries using quantile-based splits (configurable bucket_count, max_bucket_width). 3) On enqueue, attempt to place incoming requests into an existing bucket; if no good fit, either (a) create a new bucket (bounded) or (b) opportunistically pad to nearest bucket when within adaptive padding threshold. 4) Scheduler scoring: give a small latency weight and a larger padding-cost weight; score = latency_penalty*expected_wait + padding_penalty*expected_padded_tokens. 5) Add runtime knobs: bucket_count, padding_threshold_pct, quantile_smoothing_alpha, scoring_weights.

Compatibility: fully backward compatible with existing continuous-batching config; defaults are conservative and match prior behavior. Feature gated behind runtime feature flag `rbw.dynamic_batching.seqlen_v5` for canary rollouts.

Benchmarks (internal perf lab): microbench with mixed seq lengths (70% < 128, 25% 128-512, 5% > 1024) on an A100 pod: - padded tokens per-second improved by 22% vs v4 bucketing, - token cost per-inference reduced by ~14%, - p50 latency: +1% (statistically insignificant), - p95 latency: +4% (still within SLO for default config); after tuning scoring_weights we get p95 within baseline. End-to-end production canary on small customer fleet showed ~10% cost reduction with no complaint on tail latency.

Files changed (summary): runtime/batching/seqlen_bucket_manager.py (new), runtime/batching/scheduler_scoring.py (mod), runtime/batching/metrics_collector.py (mod), runtime/config/defaults.yaml (mod), tests/batching/test_seqlen_bucketing.py (new), docs/ops/dynamic_batching.md (mod).

Testing: unit tests for bucketing math and scheduler scoring; integration test that simulates mixed workload and verifies padding reduction and latency profiles; CI includes perf-canary job that runs microbench harness.

Rollout plan: behind flag -> enable on canary hosts -> monitor token-cost, p95 latency dashboards (redwood.console/dashboards/dynamic-batching) -> widen to Dedicated pools if stable -> enable by default after 2 weeks.

Notes: This implements v5 of the heuristics (see prior PRs ending 48901/v4). Followups: potential KV-cache-aware bucketing (prefer mixing requests that share KV prefixes) and GPU-kernel-aware alignment to reduce fragmentation.
